memory_candidates.content: In a layered path-surgery formalization, a 'pending forever into the past' style hypothesis typically sits on the ADMISSIBILITY half of a surgery (the walk-to-path lift and its pin-compatibility clause), never on the TYPE half (the index-map transport showing a realized type is preserved). That asymmetry is a dependency fact worth checking before declaring a complementary regime unreachable: the complementary regime fails the admissibility half for a specific, nameable reason (one pin's value moves while its distances do not), and it may supply a compensator the original regime lacks (here, an idle run below the position, which can be spliced by the same displacement so every lower pin's distance grows exactly as much as the raise cost). Phase decomposition should therefore put a two-layer gate first -- a scale-invariant arithmetic measurement of the pin deficit, then the path-level clause attempt -- rather than attempting the construction and discovering the deficit mid-proof.
